message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian lineages—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which contains all of the major groups that include both carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.  

That ancestor was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. In other words, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all Laurasiatherian mammals.
